I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`. It builds to 2364 bytes min+gzip, of which 97 bytes are my own code. `tsc` reports no errors for it. I did not compare its output against the original lodash, because lodash isn't installed here. `npm run size` on the original `src/module.ts` failed, and `tsc` only reported the missing `lodash/*` modules there, so I have no baseline number for the own-code allowance. The exported signatures are unchanged.

- **`merge`:** `applyPatch` uses `merge` from `es-toolkit`. It merges objects recursively and arrays index by index, like lodash `merge`. It also mutates `base` and returns it, as the original did. I only checked the es-toolkit source for this and did not run both versions side by side.
- **`startCase`:** `toTitle` uses `startCase` from `es-toolkit/compat`. The plain `es-toolkit` version lowercases the rest of each word, so `HELLO` would become `Hello`, while lodash keeps it as `HELLO`.
- **`truncate`:** `preview` uses `truncate` from `es-toolkit/compat`, since es-toolkit only has it there.

No lodash import remains, and I added no adapters or hand-written replacements.
